source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: All signs, between which there does not exist any familiarity in any of the modes above specified, are inconjunct and separated.

prerequisites: the preceding sign-familiarity and configuration modes
calculation_dependencies: absence of a recognized sign familiarity or configuration

condition.relationship: no familiarity in the preceding modes

normalized_rule: Classify two signs as inconjunct and separated when they share none of the preceding sign familiarities or configurations.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sign-relationship classification, not a claim about interpersonal incompatibility.
review_notes: The general definition is recorded. The source's one-sign and five-sign examples are not expanded into separate rules because their surrounding wording and editorial minor-aspect discussion require separate review. The source's sign-level 'separated' is distinct from the moving-body separation in Chapter XXVII.
transmission_notes: The main-text definition is retained, but the one-sign/five-sign examples and the surrounding editorial discussion of later minor aspects are not silently converted into an executable aspect system. The sign-level term 'separated' is kept distinct from Chapter XXVII's dynamic application/separation terminology.
